sentence: 195	Pt, ********, is a 5 month old female, diagnosed with dilated cardiomyopathy with history of  cardiac arrest and ECMO who is being referred by ******* ****** APRN for heart transplant Psychosocial Assessment.
Information for this assessment was obtained through an interview with the pt's mother, and review of the medical records.
SW spent 60 minutes of face to face time with patient and family.
Living situation:  **, ********, resides with her parents in a house[SM1] that is also shared with the paternal niece.
Mom states they have their own space in the home with the exception of sharing the ******* area.
They have a ***** for their portion of the house.
The house has central air conditioning and city water.
There are no pets.
There is no smoking in the home[SM2].

Demographics:  Mother: ****** *****  DOB: **/**/**  Age: 29  Education:  High School diploma[SM3]  Employment:  Not employed [SM4] Phone:  ***-***-**** (cell)     Father: ****** ****** **  ***: **/**/****  Age: 56  Education: GED[SM5]  Employment: *** **** Contracting  Phone: ***-***-**** (cell)     Support systems:  Mother is currently staying at bedside, while dad continues to work[SM6].
It is challenging for dad to visit as he does not have a driver's license or vehicle[SM7][SM8].
They have to rely on other people to assist them with transportation[SM9].
Mom disclosed that she and dad have been together for 1 year.
They had been together for 3 months when she became pregnant.
She states this was not a planned pregnancy.
However.
She states it has been a blessing, which led her to the name, ********.
She states that she and dad are engaged[SM10] and plan to ***** after ******** is better.
Dad has 4 other children by other relationships.
Two children are now adults and live independently.
The two younger children are ages 7 and 4.
Their mother has custody and is not currently allowing dad to have contact with them, although he does pay child support.
He is reportedly going to court to try to get visitation re-********.
Mom states that neither she nor dad have a car[SM11].
She states neither have a driver's license[SM12] either.
She disclosed that she has never pursued a driver's license.
She states dad had a driver's license.
However, he 'was not paying attention and ********** a car' about a year ago.
He left the scene.
As a result, his license was revoked and he is on probation for 3 yrs.
He has over a year remaining of this probation.
She admits that transportation to and from Gainesville will be problematic, although the aunt and niece they reside with might be able to assist.
Mom identifies the paternal aunt and niece as support persons.

She also identifies her mother, ******* ******* as a support person[SM13]. (*********@*******.***). *******, her mother works for a prison[SM14] during the week and is primarily able to help them on the weekends.
She also lives about 90 minutes away from the family.
However, Ms ******* has requested that SW send a letter to her ****** to request the ability to take time off from work to assist the family as needed.
Mom disclosed that they are *********.
She states they have no objections to blood products, transfusions, etc.
Course of illness:        ******** is a 5 month old female.
She was born via C Section.
She did not require any time in the NICU and discharged home after birth.
She was reportedly doing well at home until *** *, when she began vomiting.
Mom took her to the ED.
She quickly decompensated in the ED, going into full cardiac arrest and requiring 78 minutes of CPR.
She was cannulated for VA ECMO.
She went to cath lab for atrial septostomy.
She was decannulated on *** *.
She continued to have complications including seizures and acute kidney injury requiring PD.
She remained intubated as well.
She was transferred to our ******* for further management and possible heart transplant evaluation.
At that time, she was able to be extubated and weaned to oral medication management.
She was discharged home on **/**/**.
She began vomiting again on **** **, and was transferred back to our facility.
She is now being re-evaluated for heart transplant, and VAD support.
Financial Situation:     ******** is covered by Medicaid CMS[SM15] ********.
Mom states ******** has been approved for SSI.
However, they have not yet received any funding from this.
They do receive food ****** and WIC[SM16].
The primary source of income is dad's employment income.
Dad does not have any paid time off, and is unsure if he is eligible for FMLA.
Information on fundraising through **** was provided.
However, mom states they do not really have anyone who can assist them with this.
They were granted First Hand Foundation funding[SM17] on previous admission, and are not eligible for further funding from this organization for one year.
SW encouraged mom to call CMS[SM18] ******** case manager for assistance with meal reimbursement while ******** is admitted.
Mom states she has already called RMH regarding getting on the list.
She was advised that the second round of guests will be accepted on ****** **.
They are required to get a ******* test and present a negative result within 10 days of this date.
SW will provide mom with information on where to go for this test, as well as assist with transportation for this.
Dad is not eligible to stay there due to felony history.
Family History:     Mom states that there is diabetes, hypertension, and cancer on both sides of the family.
She states she has a maternal aunt who had a heart condition of some type that required her to be on medications for her life.
She lived into her 60's with this.
She also disclosed that the paternal grandmother had to have a pacemaker, and now lives in a nursing home.
Mom states she was referred for counseling and participated[SM19] in it briefly, but felt that she did not connect to the therapist.
She admits that she is currently stressed by the situation with ********, but denies depression or anxiety[SM20].
She states dad does not have a mental health history.
[SM21]      Mom denied any history of mental health issues[SM22], substance abuse issues, domestic violence, or history with law enforcement.
She disclosed that dad spent time in prison a long time ago, but did not want to bring those past things up and make him feel bad.
(Public record shows he has been incarcerated for drug charges including cocaine[SM23], resisting arrest, and assault both with and without a deadly weapon.
All of these were prior to the year 2000.)
There is no reported history with DCF.
[SM24]        Adherence:  ******** was discharged on several meds after previous admission.
Mom admits that she ran out of Lasix one week prior to this current admission.
There is no documentation indicating she attempted to get a refill.
[SM25]  Otherwise, she kept scheduled appointments, using Medicaid transportation.
Mom states she had attending * *** training program previously, but did not complete it.
Mom states ******** had attended all well-baby visits[SM26] and received shots until now.
She has not received 3 month shots[SM27] yet.
She also admits they were late on one of the visits due to a 'family emergency'.
Mom appears bonded with ******** and was talking to her and standing close to her throughout much of SW interaction.
Assessment and recommendations:     This is mom's first baby, although dad has had 4 previous children.
Mom presents as invested and able to advocate for her baby.
She appears bonded to her.
The family has limited financial resources[SM28], and limited support in regards to transportation.
Mom disclosed that she was hopeful that transplant would not be needed.
However, she states that she and dad are both in agreement with moving forward if it will allow her to live.
She states they feel the same in regards to the ****** VAD.

IMPRESSION:     (Low Risk - 1; Moderate Risk - 2; High Risk - 3; Severe Risk - 4)     Home Environment/Transportation -  3  Family Background & Social Support -  2  Financial/Insurance  - 2  Mental Health/Substance Abuse - 2  Involvement with *** Enforcement/Child Protection -  2  Adherence - 2  Understanding of medical situation & transplant process -  2  Health Literacy -  2  Coping Skills - 2     Total:  19 Moderate/ High Risk       The family scores as moderate/ high risk in regards to psychosocial contra-indicators to transplant.
Primary concerns are limited finances, limited support persons, limited transportation, as well as possible adherence concerns.
Recommendations are listed below:     Recommendations:  *Provide ongoing education to the family about heart transplant and post-transplant care.
Use teachback method to confirm understanding.
Provide information in writing as well.

*Provide information on Medicaid transportation to assist with transportation issues  *Provide fundraising resources to assist the family with expenses that arise secondary to transplant   * Assist family with resources to assist in coping with lengthy admission while displaced from home  *Assist in connecting mom with counseling resources   [SM1]living condition[SM2]smoking[SM3]education general[SM4]employment status[SM5]education general[SM6]employment status[SM7]**transportation access**[SM8R7]???
